section.title: Package leaflet: information for the patient

coding.display: PACKAGE LEAFLET: INFORMATION FOR THE PATIENT

code.text: PACKAGE LEAFLET: INFORMATION FOR THE PATIENT

text.div:
Synthetic example. Sakura Bloom and Sakuramil are fictitious. This text was written for a FHIR ePI demonstration and must not be used for any clinical purpose.

Sakura Bloom 20 mg film-coated tablets
Sakuramil

Read all of this leaflet carefully before you start taking this medicine because it contains important information for you.

  • Keep this leaflet. You may need to read it again.
  • If you have any further questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist.
  • This medicine has been prescribed for you only. Do not pass it on to others.
  • If you get any side effects, talk to your doctor or pharmacist. See section 4.

section.title: 1. What Sakura Bloom is and what it is used for

coding.display: 1. What Sakura Bloom is and what it is used for

code.text: 1. What Sakura Bloom is and what it is used for

text.div:
Sakura Bloom contains the active substance Sakuramil. It lowers the amount of LDL-cholesterol, sometimes called bad cholesterol, in your blood.

Sakura Bloom is used together with a cholesterol-lowering diet in adults whose cholesterol is too high when diet and exercise alone have not been enough.

section.title: 2. What you need to know before you take Sakura Bloom

coding.display: 2. What you need to know before you take Sakura Bloom

code.text: 2. What you need to know before you take Sakura Bloom

text.div:
Do not take Sakura Bloom

  • if you are allergic to Sakuramil or any of the other ingredients of this medicine (listed in section 6)
  • if you have liver disease
  • if you take ketoconazole or itraconazole (for fungal infections) or clarithromycin (for bacterial infections)
  • if you are pregnant or breast-feeding

Warnings and precautions

Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking Sakura Bloom:

  • Your doctor will do a blood test to check your liver before you start and during treatment.
  • if you have high blood pressure. Your doctor will check your blood pressure regularly.
  • if you have severe kidney problems. You should not take more than 20 mg a day.

Children and adolescents

Do not give this medicine to children and adolescents under 18 years, because it has not been studied in this age group.

Other medicines and Sakura Bloom

Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking, have recently taken or might take any other medicines, in particular:

  • diltiazem or verapamil (for high blood pressure or heart problems). You should not take more than 20 mg of Sakura Bloom a day
  • rifampicin (for tuberculosis), which can stop Sakura Bloom working well
  • warfarin (to prevent blood clots). Your doctor may check your blood more often

Sakura Bloom with food and drink

Do not drink more than 1 litre of grapefruit juice a day.

Pregnancy and breast-feeding

Do not take Sakura Bloom if you are pregnant or breast-feeding. If you could become pregnant, use effective contraception while taking this medicine.

Driving and using machines

Sakura Bloom can make some people feel dizzy. If this happens to you, do not drive or use machines.

Sakura Bloom contains lactose and sodium

If you have been told by your doctor that you have an intolerance to some sugars, contact your doctor before taking this medicine. This medicine contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per tablet, that is to say essentially sodium-free.

Always take this medicine exactly as your doctor or pharmacist has told you. Check with your doctor or pharmacist if you are not sure.

The recommended dose is one 20 mg tablet once a day. Your doctor may increase it to 40 mg once a day after at least 4 weeks. Do not take more than 40 mg a day.

Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water, with or without food, at about the same time each day.

If you take more Sakura Bloom than you should

Contact your doctor or the nearest hospital emergency department.

If you forget to take Sakura Bloom

Take the next dose at the usual time. Do not take a double dose to make up for a forgotten tablet.

If you stop taking Sakura Bloom

Talk to your doctor first, because your cholesterol may rise again.

Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them.

Stop taking Sakura Bloom and see a doctor straight away if you get swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat.

Common (may affect up to 1 in 10 people)

  • headache
  • feeling sick (nausea)
  • muscle pain

Uncommon (may affect up to 1 in 100 people)

  • dizziness
  • high blood pressure
  • raised liver enzymes in blood tests

Rare (may affect up to 1 in 1,000 people)

  • swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat (angioedema)
  • skin rash

Reporting of side effects

If you get any side effects, talk to your doctor or pharmacist. You can also report side effects directly via the national reporting system.

Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children.

Do not use this medicine after the expiry date which is stated on the carton and the blister or bottle after EXP.

This medicine does not require any special storage conditions.

Do not throw away any medicines via wastewater or household waste. Ask your pharmacist how to throw away medicines you no longer use.

section.title: 6. Contents of the pack and other information

coding.display: 6. Contents of the pack and other information

code.text: 6. Contents of the pack and other information

text.div:
What Sakura Bloom contains

  • The active substance is Sakuramil. Each film-coated tablet contains 20 mg Sakuramil.
  • The other ingredients are: tablet core: lactose monohydrate, microcrystalline cellulose, croscarmellose sodium, hydroxypropyl cellulose, magnesium stearate; film-coating: hypromellose, macrogol 6000, titanium dioxide (E171), iron oxide red (E172).

What Sakura Bloom looks like and contents of the pack

Sakura Bloom tablets are pale red, round film-coated tablets marked SB on one side and 20 on the other.

They come in cartons of 28 tablets in blisters and bottles of 30 tablets. Not all pack sizes may be marketed.

Marketing Authorisation Holder

Sakura Pharmaceuticals Europe B.V., Bloesemlaan 1, 1000 AA Amsterdam, Netherlands

Manufacturer

Aparna Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Pte. Ltd., 10 Green Road, Gulshan, Bangladesh
